title: Wolf and Oath
premise: Yara Okonkwo, exiled from her homeland for a storm she could not control, guides smugglers through the Thornfell mountains to survive. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into her hands, she discovers a route into the sealed citadel of King Aldric — whose crown has been slowly consumed by an ancient parasite called the Hollow, feeding on his mind and bending his decrees toward cruelty. Pursued by the king's oathbound hunters and shadowed by the map's dying guardian, a disgraced knight named Cassel, Yara must decide whether justice outside the law is worth the storm it will cost her. In the final confrontation beneath the thirteenth moon, Yara calls the storm she once feared, tearing the Hollow from the king at the price of her exile becoming permanent — and finds, in Cassel and the smugglers who stood by her, the belonging she thought she had lost forever.
about_author: Theo Sterling is the pen name of a former mountain guide who traded trail maps for story maps after a near-fatal winter in the passes. They write fantasy about outsiders, broken oaths, and the weather that lives inside people.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Leading a caravan through a hidden pass, Yara demonstrates her mastery of the Thornfell and her careful distance from her own storm-magic. A checkpoint ambush forces her to use a flicker of power, reminding her why she was exiled. Beat: competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Blood on the Snowline
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A dying courier collapses at her fire, pressing a wax-sealed map into her hands and gasping the words 'thirteenth moon' before the king's hunters arrive. Yara escapes by triggering a rockslide. Beat: fear — she wanted no part of this.

chapters.title: The Map That Refuses
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Examining the map in a smuggler's den, Yara finds it marked in storm-script only she can read, and it seems to shift when she lies to herself about burning it. The smugglers urge her to sell it. Beat: reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: The Knight Without a Banner
chapters.summary: Cassel's POV. Cassel, the courier's sworn protector, tracks Yara intending to reclaim the map by force, but witnesses her spare a hunter's life and hesitates. He follows her instead, unannounced. Beat: a broken oath seeking a new purpose.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: King Aldric's POV. In the citadel, Aldric wakes with blood on his hands and a decree he doesn't remember signing. The Hollow whispers that it is his strength. Beat: dread — the horror of a mind being eaten from inside.

chapters.title: Road of Thorns
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Ambushed by hunters on the mountain road, Yara is saved when Cassel reveals himself and fights at her side. They form an uneasy truce: he knows the citadel, she knows the passes. Beat: grudging alliance.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Yara and Cassel shelter in a village erased from royal records by one of the Hollow's decrees. Its people have forgotten their own history — the parasite feeds on memory, not just minds. Beat: the stakes become human.

chapters.title: Storm-Script Rising
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The map leads them to a hermit storm-caller, Mother Ije, who recognizes the script: it was written by Yara's own exiled order. The Hollow has hunted storm-callers for centuries. Beat: her exile was engineered.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Oath
chapters.summary: Captain Vess's POV. The hunters' captain, bound by an unbreakable oath-spell, closes in. Vess begins to suspect the decrees she enforces come from something other than her king. Beat: loyalty cracking under evidence.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Cassel's POV. Cassel confesses his role in the purge of Yara's order years ago; Yara nearly abandons him. Mother Ije's divination reveals the moon's thirteenth turn seals the Hollow permanently into the crown. Beat: betrayal, forgiveness deferred.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Aldric, surfacing briefly, smuggles a message to Yara through a loyal servant: he begs to be unbound, even if it kills him. The Hollow punishes him with a purge of the capital. Beat: the king as prisoner.

chapters.title: Pass of Ash
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The only remaining route to the citadel runs through a pass the Hollow burned decades ago. Vess's hunters corner them; Mother Ije stays behind to hold the line and dies buying them hours. Beat: grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Price of the Gate
chapters.summary: Yara and Cassel's alternating POV. To open the citadel's hidden gate, the map demands a memory as payment. Cassel offers his — the last memory of his brother — and Yara realizes she would have given hers. Beat: sacrifice deepening the bond.

chapters.title: Beneath the Citadel
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the tunnels below the throne, they find the bones of every storm-caller the Hollow consumed — including, Yara realizes, the courier who started her journey. Beat: horror and inheritance.

chapters.title: The Servant's Gambit
chapters.summary: The loyal servant Sera's POV. Sera smuggles Yara and Cassel into the palace as plague-bearers, then is caught by Vess. Instead of executing her, Vess demands the truth. Beat: an enemy turning witness.

chapters.title: Audience with a Ghost
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara reaches Aldric and speaks with the man beneath the parasite for the first time — he remembers her order, remembers sparing her as a child. The Hollow discovers them. Beat: hope, then catastrophe.

chapters.title: Chains of the Crown
chapters.summary: Cassel's POV. Cassel is captured covering Yara's escape and brought before the Hollow, which wears Aldric's face and offers to restore Cassel's honor if he betrays her. Cassel refuses. Beat: the oath finally kept.

chapters.title: Vess's Choice
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Shown proof of the Hollow by Sera, Vess breaks her oath-spell at terrible cost — the spell burns her sword arm — and opens the hunters' cells for Cassel. Beat: justice chosen over law.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Night
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. With one night before the thirteenth turn, Yara, Cassel, Vess, and the smugglers storm the throne room. Mother Ije's final gift — a storm bottled in glass — shatters in Yara's hands. Beat: the calm before the tempest.

chapters.title: The Storm She Feared
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara faces the Hollow and calls the full storm she was exiled for, tearing it from the crown while Aldric, lucid for one last minute, holds the parasite's attention. The storm nearly consumes her — until Cassel anchors her. Beat: climax, power embraced not corrupted.

chapters.title: What the Crown Weighs
chapters.summary: Cassel's POV. The Hollow is destroyed; Aldric, freed but dying, abdicates to a council that includes the forgotten village's survivors. Vess is pardoned; Cassel refuses a knighthood, choosing the road instead. Beat: bittersweet victory.

chapters.title: Every Road Home
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Exile formally ended, Yara realizes home was never a place on the map. She rides out with Cassel and the smugglers, storm-script now writing itself in her palm — a new road, unwritten. Beat: belonging found, journey continuing.
